CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
SPECIMEN TYPE: Uncultured placental tissue
SPECIMEN ID: [redacted ID]
DATE COLLECTED: [redacted date]
DATE RECEIVED: [redacted date]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Fetal specimen submitted for chromosomal analysis

TEST PERFORMED
Oligonucleotide Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)

METHODOLOGY
Array CGH: DNA extracted from uncultured placental material was analyzed using the GeneTech oligonucleotide array platform (design DT8530) containing approximately 60,000 probes distributed across the genome with a median resolution of 120kb. Analysis was performed using GenomeView software with reference to the GRCh37/hg19 human genome assembly.

QF-PCR: Multiplex QF-PCR analysis was performed for rapid aneuploidy detection of chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X and Y using fluorescently labeled primers for polymorphic STR markers.

RESULTS

Array CGH: arr(1-22,X,Y)x2
No copy number imbalances detected

The array analysis shows a balanced male chromosome complement with no deletions or duplications of known pathogenic significance identified. All autosomes (chromosomes 1-22) and sex chromosomes (XY) show normal copy number.

QF-PCR: Normal male pattern
No evidence of trisomy 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, or 22
No evidence of triploidy
Sex chromosome complement: XY

INTERPRETATION
No imbalances of known fully penetrant pathogenicity were detected by array CGH analysis. The results are consistent with a normal male chromosome complement. QF-PCR analysis showed no evidence of common aneuploidies or triploidy.

These findings indicate no chromosomal abnormality that would explain the clinical presentation.

TECHNICAL LIMITATIONS
This array has a median resolution of 120kb and will not detect:
- Balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%)
- Copy number variants smaller than the resolution of the array
- Point mutations or small insertions/deletions
- Methylation abnormalities or uniparental disomy

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is needed on this sample based on current findings.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
